html:
An earthquake of magnitude 6.8 struck the High Atlas mountains of Morocco, southwest of Marrakesh, late on 8 September 2023. It killed nearly 3,000 people, mostly in mountain villages of the Al Haouz province.

The villages, of mud brick and stone and reached by steep roads, collapsed, and help was slow to reach them. In Marrakesh the old medina was damaged. The 12th century mosque at Tinmel, where the Almohad movement of Ibn Tumart began, was largely destroyed.

It was the deadliest earthquake in Morocco since the Agadir earthquake of 1960. The government planned to rebuild the villages, and Moroccans gave in large numbers. See also Morocco.
sum: An earthquake of magnitude 6.8 struck the High Atlas mountains of Morocco, southwest of Marrakesh, late on 8 September 2023. It killed nearly 3,000 people, mostly in mountain villages of the Al Haouz province.
